title: Ownership in function signatures
description:
The starter does not compile: the tests expect `report` and `add_suffix` to **give the vector back** after using it, so that the caller owns it again. Fix the **signatures** (and bodies) using only ownership: a function that takes a `String` or a `Vec` owns it, may change it, and can hand it back by returning it.

```rust
fn report(names: Vec<String>) -> (String, Vec<String>)        // ("3 names: Ada, Grace, Linus", the same vector); "no names" when empty
fn longest(a: String, b: String) -> String                   // the longer text (the first on a tie); the other one is dropped
fn shout(text: String) -> String                             // the text upper-cased, with "!" added
fn add_suffix(names: Vec<String>, suffix: &str) -> Vec<String>   // the vector with suffix appended to every name, in order
```

Read the tests to see how each function is called, and where they use `.clone()` to keep a value they still need.
hints: A function that owns a value can return it, alone or in a tuple next to its result: `fn measure(s: String) -> (usize, String) { (s.len(), s) }` is called as `let (n, s) = measure(s);`, and the caller owns `s` again.
To change a value you own, rebind it as mutable with `let mut name = name;`. `for name in names` moves the names out of the vector one at a time: change each one and `push` it onto a new `Vec`.
